lesson.applicability: Moving conditional mathematical or numerical results between worker briefs, displays, typed claims and public input contracts.
lesson.cause: Related bounds and separately maintained claim projections were treated as one repaired statement.
lesson.correction: Match each bound and its exact premises across proof, display, structured claim and consuming input contract. Keep legitimate per-bound domains separate; recheck each affected projection and carry unresolved assumptions forward.
lesson.counterexample: R3-OBJ-04 finds mu>=0 repaired but the weighted embedding claim still omits 0<=theta<=1/192. Its sup-rate bound correctly has the different domain 0<=theta<1/128.
lesson.evidence_excerpt: The round-2 B1 acceptance required both.
lesson.exceptions: Different bounds may have different valid domains; do not blindly force all consumers into the smallest range. A separately justified stronger result may remove a premise. Excluded inputs do not refute a correctly restricted claim.
lesson.failed_claim: Repairing a missing premise in the proof or display also repairs every structured claim and consumer.
lesson.verification: Read R3-OBJ-04 and C2, then R4-OBJ-03 and R5-OBJ-03 reporting the range repair. The earlier R2 mu restriction remains historical context. No Meron consumer, analytic proof or Lean compilation was executed in this digestion.

predicate: Each specific bound retains its own used hypotheses in every affected claim and consumer.
response: Repair the affected projection or narrow that bound; preserve other valid domains and retain an unproved extension as open.
trigger: Before presenting or consuming a bound or conditional result
